document.title: Deputy Secretary Armitage-Mamoud Phone Call – September 18, 2001 (State 161279)
document.publisher: National Security Archive (GWU), "No-Go" Tribal Areas Became Basis for Afghan Insurgency Documents Show
document.note: [Confidential] ISI Director Mahmoud Ahmed flew to Afghanistan on September 17 aboard a U.S. government aircraft to meet Mullah Omar. He relayed three U.S. conditions: hand over UBL, hand over his 13 top lieutenants, and close terrorist training camps. Mahmoud says the Taliban response was not negative on all points and that Afghan Islamic leaders were in deep introspection.

persons.name: Mahmud Ahmed
persons.role: Director General of Pakistan's ISI (Lieutenant General)

mentions.quote: PAKISTAN ISI DIRECTOR LIEUTENANT GENERAL MAMOUD AND THE DEPUTY SECRETARY SPOKE BY TELEPHONE FOR 5 MINUTES ON 18 SEPTEMBER
HE HAD THE OPPORTUNITY TO MEET WITH ISLAMIC LEADER MULLAH OMAR, AS WELL AS OTHER GOVERNMENT AND JUDICIARY MINISTRY OFFICIALS
HE AND HIS WIFE WERE BOTH GRATEFUL TO HAVE THE SAFE AND COMFORTABLE TRAVEL AFFORDED THEM
CLASSIFIED BY RICHARD L. ARMITAGE, DEPUTY SECRETARY OF STATE
DEPUTY SECRETARY ARMITAGE THANKED GENERAL MAMOUD AND ADDED THAT HE HOPED THE AFGHAN LEADERS HAD THE WISDOM TO LISTEN
MEET WITH ISLAMIC LEADER MULLAH OMAR
HE FRAMED THE DECISION TO MULLAH OMAR AND THE OTHER AFGHANS AS ESSENTIALLY CHOOSING BETWEEN ONE MAN AND HIS SAFE HAVEN

persons.name: Usama bin Ladin
persons.role: al-Qa'ida leader whose handover to the US/ICJ was demanded

mentions.quote: THEY MUST HAND-OVER UBL TO THE UNITED STATES
HAND-OVER OR EXTRADITE THE 13 TOP LIEUTENANTS/ASSOCIATES OF UBL
HE IS STAYING IN VERY CLOSE CONTACT WITH US AMBASSADOR CHAMBERLIN

key_claims: Pakistan's ISI chief personally conveyed US demands to Mullah Omar in Kandahar-era Afghanistan days after 9/11.
The demands: hand over UBL to the US or ICJ, hand over his 13 top lieutenants, and close all terrorist training camps.
Mamoud added a fourth condition on his own: open training sites to neutral international inspectors.
The Taliban response was 'not negative on all these points' and a Grand Council of Elders was to decide.
Mamoud framed the choice as one man and his safe haven versus 25 million Afghans.
The US government provided aircraft for Mamoud and his wife's return to Pakistan.
